rationale: This is a one-operator respecification (IND_ZSCORE→IND_RANK on the leverage leg) of the archive's best signal, and making both legs monotone ranks reintroduces the expensiveness main effect, so a strong FMB slope would largely restate the known value premium rather than validate the claimed dear-and-levered interaction.

An unweighted rank-average of two separately documented main effects (sales-to-price value and net leverage) is close to trivial as a cross-theme signal, and SUMRANK implements an average rather than the "either condition suffices" logic the hypothesis states (which would require MAX).

A coherent and correctly signed cross-tail generalization of the archive's hidden-claims channel, though it is mechanically close to (hidden-claims main effect minus the existing cheap-tail signal), so the incremental information may be modest and partly attributable to the non-current-liability level itself.

Internally consistent (the centering does keep both spread legs inside the expensive tail, and the NEG makes high values = expensive-and-untaxed = negative sign), but txt/at is a fairly direct profitability proxy, so this risks being the well-known expensive-and-unprofitable "junk growth" effect that RMW may absorb.

target_name: Which Risk Is Paid For Inside Value
rationale: The financial-versus-operating risk wedge is a genuinely novel, sign-consistent formalization of the contradiction between two prior archive results, with the caveat that it is approximately the difference of those two signals and so a strong alpha may be arithmetic rather than new information.

target_name: Premium Over Assets With Net Claims
rationale: Legs are mechanically anti-correlated (high liabilities depress book equity and hence ME/at), so the intended dear-and-encumbered corner is thinly populated and the composite largely collapses to an expensive-enterprise-value-per-asset sort, i.e., a denominator swap on the archive's best signal rather than a distinct mechanism.
